source.title: Longest-edge n-section algorithms: Properties and open problems

evidence.quote: Summary: In this paper we survey all known (including own recent results) properties of the longest-edge \(n\)-section algorithms. These algorithms (in classical and recently designed conforming form) are nowadays used in many applications, including finite element simulations, computer graphics, etc. as a reliable tool for controllable mesh generation. In addition, we present a list of open problems arising in and around this topic.

trace.notes: Treated zbMATH 6496054 as a resolver, extracted the exact-work identity from the zbMATH record, and resolved it to DOI 10.1016/j.cam.2015.03.046 / PII S0377042715001995 for the article 'Longest-edge n-section algorithms: Properties and open problems'. Crossref exposed Elsevier text-mining links for the same DOI, and OpenAlex identified the same work plus a repository handle candidate at https://accedacris.ulpgc.es/jspui/handle/10553/56548.

No readable PDF or HTML full-text artifact for this exact work could be recovered. The ScienceDirect article and PDF endpoints returned access-blocking 403/captcha responses, the AccedaCris repository landing and OAI endpoints failed with 503 responses or timeouts from this environment, and the Elsevier content API returned only minimized core metadata rather than the article body. Because no readable primary source artifact was obtained, no doc_map could be constructed.

Moved the source to needs_review under the source-adequacy gate because the available zbMATH, Crossref, OpenAlex, and minimized Elsevier API records are metadata-only for extraction purposes and do not expose the paper's verbatim open-problem statements. Extracting questions from those resolver records alone would violate the no-new-facts and source-adequacy requirements.
